problemStatement.formal: Assess which heat-kernel and representation-theoretic techniques from exactly solvable two-dimensional Yang-Mills theory can inform, but not solve, higher-dimensional Yang-Mills questions.
problemStatement.plain: Survey the boundary between solvable 2D Yang-Mills heat-kernel methods and the harder 3D/4D theories, recording which mechanisms formalize cleanly and where the analogy breaks.
whyMatters: Prevents the 2D exact solution from being mistaken for progress on the 4D Millennium Prize problem.
Captures concrete formal objects such as heat-kernel decay and Casimir scaling in a reusable Lean entry.
Documents why topological 3D behavior and dynamical 4D behavior require different proof strategies.

proven: The entry replaces vacuous axioms with concrete definitions and proven theorems for the 2D model.
Heat-kernel terms decay exponentially with area in the formalized model.
For the SU(2) toy setting, the adjoint-to-fundamental Casimir scaling ratio is formalized as 16/9.
The partition-function model records decay from the zero-area value toward trivial-representation dominance.
open: No transfer from these 2D identities to a 4D constructive Yang-Mills existence proof is established.
The 3D Chern-Simons/topological regime is structurally different from area-dependent 2D Yang-Mills.
The physical 4D mass gap remains outside this formalized survey.
knownResults.goal: Keep this as a scoped survey/formal-toy-model bridge: useful for 2D heat-kernel mechanics, not a claimed solution path for 4D Yang-Mills.

insights: 2D Yang-Mills is exactly solvable via heat kernel representation decomposition
3D: Wilson loops depend on knot type not area (Chern-Simons = topological)
4D: theory has physical degrees of freedom, no exact solution possible
Dimensional reduction S¹×Σ → Σ connects 3D to 2D at high temperature
Gross-Taylor expansion connects 2D large-N to string theory
Replaced 10 vacuous axioms (3 definition-as-axiom, 7 stating True) with 8 concrete definitions and 16 proven theorems
Heat kernel terms provably decay exponentially with area — this is the 2D mass gap mechanism
Casimir scaling ratio sigma_adj/sigma_fund = 16/9 proved exactly for SU(2)
Partition function provably decays from Z(0)=14 to trivial rep dominance at large area
